question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Hard nut to crack
option_3: A situation that can be altered
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. A problem difficult to solve.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Hard nut to crack" means a problem, task or person that is very difficult to deal with or solve. (एक मुश्किल समस्या)
◦ Example: Convincing him to change his mind is a hard nut to crack.

• The idiom compares a difficult problem to a nut with a very tough shell — just as a hard-shelled nut takes great effort to crack open, a difficult problem takes great effort to solve.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: To leave an effect (प्रभाव छोड़ना): To make a lasting impression on someone or something; unrelated to difficulty.

• Option 3: A situation that can be altered: Describes something changeable, which is the opposite sense of a "hard nut to crack" — such problems are not easily altered.

• Option 4: To bid farewell (विदाई देना): To say goodbye to someone; has nothing to do with difficulty.

NOTE

• Other idioms meaning "difficult": "A tough nut to crack" (same meaning, used interchangeably), "An uphill task", and "A Herculean task" (a task requiring great strength or effort).

• Do not confuse with idioms of ease, such as "A piece of cake" or "Child's play", which mean the exact opposite — something very easy.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
Sanyukta has to bake fifty-one cakes for the anniversary party.
option_1: Fifty-one cakes will be baked by Sanyukta for the anniversary party.
option_2: Fifty-one cakes had to be baken by Sanyukta for the anniversary party.
option_3: Fifty-one cakes have to be baked by Sanyukta for the anniversary party.
option_4: Fifty-one cakes has to be baked by Sanyukta for the anniversary party.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Fifty-one cakes have to be baked by Sanyukta for the anniversary party.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "Sanyukta has to bake fifty-one cakes" uses the structure "Subject + has to + V1 + Object", which expresses present obligation/necessity.

• Rule — Passive voice with "has to / have to":
◦ Active: Subject + has/have to + V1 + Object
◦ Passive: Object + has/have to + be + V3 + by + Subject
◦ The auxiliary "has to" or "have to" agrees with the new subject (the object of the active sentence), not with the original subject.

• Applying the rule: the object "fifty-one cakes" becomes the subject of the passive sentence. Since "cakes" is plural, the auxiliary must be "have to" (not "has to"); the verb "bake" becomes the past participle "baked"; and "Sanyukta" becomes the agent with "by".
◦ Passive: Fifty-one cakes have to be baked by Sanyukta for the anniversary party.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "will be baked" changes the sense of obligation ("has to") into simple future tense, which alters the original meaning.

• Option 2 is incorrect on two counts: "had to" wrongly shifts the sentence into the past tense, and "baken" is not a standard/correct past participle of "bake" — the correct past participle is "baked".

• Option 4 is incorrect because "has to be baked" wrongly uses the singular auxiliary "has" with the plural subject "fifty-one cakes"; subject-verb agreement requires "have".

NOTE

• With modal-like obligation expressions (has to/have to, is to/are to, is going to/are going to), the auxiliary in the passive must still agree in number with the new (passive) subject, exactly as it would in the active voice with the original subject.

• Common irregular past participles that are frequently tested: bake–baked (regular, NOT "baken"), take–taken, break–broken, speak–spoken, wake–woken.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Submisive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Submisive" is incorrectly spelt. The correct spelling is "Submissive", with a double "s" in the middle (sub + missive), meaning ready to obey others without resistance.

• Spelling key: SUB + MISS + IVE. Remember the doubled "s" — the same doubling appears in the related noun "submission" and the verb "submit" (which doubles its final letter before "-ed"/"-ing": submitted, submitting).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Validity" — correctly spelt; means the quality of being legally or logically sound.

• Option 3: "Kaleidoscope" — correctly spelt; a toy or instrument showing changing patterns of colour.

• Option 4: "Animation" — correctly spelt; the technique of making inanimate objects appear to move, or the quality of being lively.

NOTE

• Other commonly confused doubled-consonant words in SSC exams: "possession", "commission", "permission", "aggression" and "assassin" — all doubling the consonant before the ending.

• A useful check: whenever a word derives from a root ending in "-mit" (submit, permit, commit, transmit), the noun form usually doubles the "s" before "-ion/-ive" (submission/submissive, permission, commission, transmission).

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the italicised group of words in the given sentence.
The prime minister paid tributes to the martyrs by laying circular arrangement of flowers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. wreaths.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "wreath" means an arrangement of flowers, leaves or stems fastened in a ring/circular shape, typically used for decoration or, as here, laid at a memorial as a mark of respect. (शोक-श्रद्धांजलि हेतु फूलों का गोलाकार गुच्छा)
◦ Example: Dignitaries laid a wreath at the war memorial to honour the soldiers.

• The phrase "circular arrangement of flowers" used for paying tribute to martyrs is a standard description of a wreath — the circular shape distinguishes it from an ordinary bunch of flowers.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "buds" (कलियाँ): Unopened flowers; not necessarily arranged, and has no circular sense.

• Option 2: "posies" (छोटे फूलों का गुच्छा): A small, informal bunch of flowers; not circular and not associated with paying tribute at memorials.

• Option 3: "bouquets" (फूलों का गुलदस्ता): An attractively arranged bunch of flowers, typically handheld; describes a general arrangement, not specifically a circular one.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutions often confused: "garland" (a ring of flowers worn around the neck or hung as decoration) and "wreath" (a circular arrangement typically laid down, especially at memorials/graves) are close but contextually distinct — garlands are worn/hung, wreaths are laid.

• Other flower-related one-word substitutes tested by SSC: "posy" (small bunch), "nosegay" (a small bunch of sweet-smelling flowers), "corsage" (a small bouquet worn by a woman).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.
The village fair was cancelled due to incessant rains.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Sporadic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Incessant" means continuing without pause or interruption; unceasing. (लगातार, अनवरत)
◦ Example: The baby's incessant crying kept them awake all night.

• "Sporadic" means occurring occasionally or at irregular intervals; not continuous. (कभी-कभार होने वाला) — this is the direct opposite of "incessant", making it the correct antonym.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Insistent" means persistently repeating a demand or opinion — it is close in sense to "incessant" (persistent), not its opposite.

• Option 2: "Daily" means happening every day, which does not capture the idea of continuity vs. intermittency being tested here, and is not a standard antonym of "incessant".

• Option 4: "Continual" is actually a near-synonym of "incessant" (something happening frequently or repeatedly without stopping), not its antonym.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "incessant": constant, perpetual, ceaseless, unremitting, unrelenting.

• Other antonyms of "incessant"/"continual": intermittent, occasional, periodic, fitful — all of these, like "sporadic", describe something that stops and starts rather than continuing without a break.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
The practice of writing dictionaries
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Lexicography.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Lexicography" means the practice/profession of compiling dictionaries. (शब्दकोश-निर्माण/संकलन का कार्य)
◦ Example: She has spent thirty years in lexicography, compiling dictionaries for several Indian languages.

• The word comes from Greek "lexikon" (word-book) + "graphein" (to write) — literally "word-writing", which matches "the practice of writing dictionaries" exactly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Anthropology" (मानवशास्त्र): The scientific study of human beings, their societies and cultures — unrelated to dictionaries.

• Option 3: "Photography" (छायांकन): The art or practice of taking photographs — completely unrelated.

• Option 4: "Philology" (भाषा-विज्ञान): The study of the structure, historical development and relationships of languages; related to language study broadly, but not specifically the writing/compiling of dictionaries.

NOTE

• Do not confuse "Lexicography" (the practice of compiling dictionaries) with "Lexicology" (the branch of linguistics that studies words and their meanings) — the person who compiles a dictionary is a "lexicographer".

• Other "-graphy" one-word substitutes tested by SSC: "Cartography" (map-making), "Choreography" (arrangement of dance steps), "Biography" (an account of a person's life written by someone else).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Trivial
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Significant.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Trivial" means of little value or importance; insignificant, trifling. (महत्वहीन, तुच्छ)
◦ Example: They argued over a trivial matter that did not deserve so much attention.

• "Significant" means important enough to be worthy of attention; noteworthy. (महत्वपूर्ण) — this is the direct opposite of "trivial" in the sense of importance, making it the correct antonym.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Huge" means very large in size — this is an antonym of "small", not of "trivial" (which is about importance, not size).

• Option 3: "Heavy" means having great weight — again a size/weight-based word, unrelated to the importance-based meaning of "trivial".

• Option 4: "Light" means having little weight — this would actually work as a loose antonym of "heavy", not of "trivial".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "trivial": trifling, petty, negligible, insignificant, minor.

• Other antonyms of "trivial": important, momentous, substantial, weighty (used figuratively to mean "important", e.g. "a weighty matter") — note how "weighty" can mean important, while "heavy" (option 3) is used only literally for physical weight.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.
I object the false claims made against me.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. assent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Here "object" is used as a verb meaning to express opposition or disapproval; to protest against something. (आपत्ति करना, विरोध करना)
◦ Example: The lawyer objected to the question on the grounds that it was misleading.

• "Assent" means to agree to or accept something, especially after consideration. (सहमति देना) — this is the direct opposite of expressing opposition, making it the correct antonym.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "ease" means to make something less severe or difficult, or to relax — unrelated to agreement or opposition.

• Option 3: "restore" means to bring something back to its former state or position — unrelated to the sense of agreeing/objecting.

• Option 4: "ascertain" means to find out or establish something with certainty — a verb of discovery, not of agreement.

NOTE

• "Object" can be a noun (a thing, pronounced OB-ject) or a verb (to oppose, pronounced ob-JECT) — here it is used as a verb, so the antonym must also express agreement/consent, such as "assent", "agree", "consent", or "approve".

• Other synonyms of "object" (verb): protest, oppose, disapprove, dissent.

• Other antonyms of "object" (verb): approve, comply, concur, acquiesce.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom for the given underlined segment in the sentence.
Riya always considers sincerity, devotion and dedication as the highest priority of a good employee.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. First and foremost.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "First and foremost" means most importantly; before anything else; of the highest priority. (सबसे पहले, सर्वोपरि)
◦ Example: First and foremost, a doctor must be compassionate towards patients.

• This idiom directly matches the meaning of "highest priority" in the sentence, which is why it can replace the underlined segment without changing the meaning.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Fair and square" (ईमानदारी से): In an honest, straightforward manner, without cheating — unrelated to priority.
◦ Example: He won the match fair and square.

• Option 2: "Ever and anon" (कभी-कभी): From time to time; occasionally — refers to frequency, not priority.

• Option 3: "Free and easy" (लापरवाह, बेतकल्लुफ): Relaxed, casual and informal in manner — unrelated to priority or importance.

NOTE

• Other idioms expressing "importance/priority" often asked in SSC: "Top priority", "Of paramount importance", "Uppermost in one's mind".

• Note the difference between similar-sounding paired idioms: "fair and square" (honest), "free and easy" (casual), "first and foremost" (most important), and "ever and anon" (occasionally) — each pair has a distinct, fixed meaning that must be memorised individually.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym for the highlighted word.
This is credible information provided by the informer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. dependable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Credible" means able to be believed; convincing and trustworthy. (विश्वसनीय)
◦ Example: The witness gave a credible account of the accident.

• "Dependable" means trustworthy and reliable. (भरोसेमंद) — this is the closest match in meaning to "credible", making it the correct synonym.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "commendable" means deserving praise — refers to something praiseworthy, not something believable.

• Option 3: "detachable" means able to be removed or separated — completely unrelated in meaning to "credible".

• Option 4: "digestible" means able to be digested (of food) or easily understood (figuratively) — not a match for "believable/trustworthy".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "credible": believable, plausible, convincing, trustworthy, reliable.

• Do not confuse "credible" (believable) with the similar-looking words "credulous" (too ready to believe things; gullible) and "creditable" (deserving acknowledgement or praise) — these three are frequently tested together in SSC vocabulary questions.

question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. It is not a walker's paradise. So walking is not a fashionable pastime here.
B. London is known for its hectic face, frenzied movements, high decibels and dust kicked by the speeding vehicles.
C. On the contrary, life in the countryside is laid back and easy paced. Unless it is raining, people set out for walk.
D. For these reasons, Max never went out for a walk, nor did anyone ask him to accompany.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. BADC.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sentence B is the ideal opener as it introduces the topic and setting — London — describing its hectic pace, which is a general, independent statement suited to beginning a paragraph.

• Sentence A follows B logically: because London is hectic and crowded (as stated in B), "it" (London) is not a walker's paradise, so walking is not fashionable there — the pronoun "it" refers back to London in B.

• Sentence D follows next: "for these reasons" (the reasons given in A — walking not being fashionable) explains why the character Max never went out for a walk.

• Sentence C concludes the paragraph with a contrast ("On the contrary") — shifting from the hectic city (B, A, D) to the laid-back countryside where people do walk, unless it rains.
◦ Logical chain: B (London is hectic) → A (so walking isn't fashionable there) → D (so Max never walked) → C (contrast: countryside people do walk).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. BADC.

Additional Information

• Option 1 (ADCB) is incorrect because it begins with "It is not a walker's paradise" — the pronoun "It" has no antecedent if the paragraph does not first establish that the subject is London, making this an illogical opening.

• Option 3 (DCAB) is incorrect because it opens with "For these reasons, Max never went out for a walk" — "these reasons" cannot refer to anything, since no reasons have yet been stated at the start of the paragraph.

• Option 4 (CADB) is incorrect because it opens with "On the contrary" — a contrast word cannot begin a paragraph, since there is nothing yet stated for it to contrast with.

NOTE

• In para-jumble questions, always locate the sentence that can stand independently as an opener (it should not contain pronouns like "it/this/these" without a clear antecedent, nor start with contrast/conclusion words like "however/on the contrary/therefore").

• Words like "for these reasons", "on the contrary", "therefore", "however" are strong linking clues — they almost always signal a sentence that must follow another, never one that can open the paragraph.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
My father is reading the newspaper.
option_1: The newspaper is being read by my father.
option_2: The newspaper happens to be read by my father.
option_3: The newspaper was being read by my father.
option_4: My father likes reading the newspaper.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. The newspaper is being read by my father.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "My father is reading the newspaper" is in the Present Continuous Tense (Subject + is/am/are + V-ing + Object).

• Rule — Present Continuous Tense:
◦ Active: Subject + is/am/are + V-ing + Object
◦ Passive: Object + is/am/are + being + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "the newspaper" becomes the subject; since it is singular, the auxiliary is "is"; "being" is added to preserve the continuous sense; the verb "read" becomes the past participle "read" (V3 form, same spelling as V1); and "my father" becomes the agent with "by".
◦ Passive: The newspaper is being read by my father.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 is incorrect because "happens to be read" introduces a sense of coincidence that is not present in the original sentence and is not the standard passive form of the present continuous.

• Option 3 is incorrect because "was being read" is the passive form of the Past Continuous Tense, not the Present Continuous Tense of the original sentence.

• Option 4 is incorrect because "My father likes reading the newspaper" changes the entire meaning of the sentence (from an ongoing action to a general preference) and is not even in the passive voice.

NOTE

• The verb "read" is unusual in that its past tense and past participle (V2 and V3) are spelled identically to the base form (V1) — "read/read/read" — though the pronunciation of V2/V3 changes to "red".

• Continuous tenses always retain the auxiliary "being" in the passive voice: Present Continuous → is/am/are + being + V3; Past Continuous → was/were + being + V3.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
He described about the scenery yesterday.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. described the scenery.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "describe" is a transitive verb and takes a direct object without any preposition — it is never followed by "about".

• Rule: Certain verbs (describe, discuss, resemble, reach, marry, obey, accompany, etc.) are directly followed by their object and must NOT be followed by a preposition such as "about", "to", "with", etc.
◦ Correct: describe the scenery / discuss the matter / resemble his father.
◦ Incorrect: describe about the scenery / discuss about the matter / resemble with his father.

• Since the sentence is about a completed action "yesterday" (Simple Past Tense), the verb must be in its past form "described", directly followed by the object "the scenery", with no preposition.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "described about the scenary" is incorrect for two reasons — the unnecessary preposition "about" after "described", and the misspelling "scenary" (correct spelling: "scenery").

• Option 3: "describing about the scenery" is incorrect because the sentence requires the simple past tense form "described" (matching "yesterday"), not the present participle "describing"; it also wrongly retains "about".

• Option 4: "describe the scenery" is incorrect because it uses the base form "describe" instead of the past tense "described", which does not agree with the time marker "yesterday".

NOTE

• Other verbs commonly tested for the "no preposition after verb" rule in SSC exams: reach (not reach at/to), marry (not marry with), resemble (not resemble with), obey (not obey to), accompany (not accompany with), discuss (not discuss about), enter (not enter into a room, though "enter into an agreement" is correct idiomatically).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Robbust.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Robbust" is incorrectly spelt. The correct spelling is "Robust", with a single "b", meaning strong and healthy, or sturdy in construction.

• Spelling key: RO + BUST — only one "b", unlike words such as "rubbish" or "hobby" which genuinely double their consonants. A useful memory aid is that "Robust" contains the word "bust" (as in a sturdy statue/bust), spelled with just one "b".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Oligopoly" — correctly spelt; a market condition dominated by a small number of sellers.

• Option 2: "Xylophone" — correctly spelt; a musical instrument played by striking wooden bars.

• Option 3: "Zenith" — correctly spelt; the highest point or peak of something.

NOTE

• Commonly misspelt words in SSC exams that add an unnecessary doubled consonant (just like "Robbust" for "Robust"): "comitted" for "committed" (needs double t, not the reverse error but similarly tested), "acommodate" for "accommodate", and "adress" for "address" — always double-check whether a consonant should or should not be doubled.

• Related word: the noun form of "robust" is "robustness".

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
My younger brother were attending a short-term computer course these days.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. were attending.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject of the sentence, "My younger brother", is a singular subject (third person singular).

• Rule — Subject-Verb Agreement: A singular subject must take a singular auxiliary verb. For the Present Continuous Tense, a singular subject takes "was" (in past continuous) or "is" (in present continuous), while a plural subject takes "were"/"are".

• Since the sentence uses the time marker "these days", it should be in the Present Continuous Tense, requiring the singular auxiliary "is". The given segment wrongly uses the plural auxiliary "were" with the singular subject "brother" — the correct form should be "is attending".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "My younger brother" is grammatically correct as a singular noun phrase functioning as the subject; it contains no error.

• Option 3: "a short-term computer course" is a correctly formed noun phrase acting as the object of the verb; it contains no error.

• Option 4: "these days" is a correctly used adverbial time phrase indicating an action happening around the present time; it contains no error.

NOTE

• Time expressions like "these days", "nowadays", "at present", "currently" typically signal the Present Continuous Tense, which requires "is/am/are + V-ing" agreeing in number and person with the subject.

• Common singular subjects that are mistakenly paired with plural verbs: each, every, everyone, everybody, nobody, either, neither, and singular collective nouns like team, family, brother/sister when referring to one person — all of these require a singular verb.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
I worked hard so that I might success.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. that I might succeed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The clause "so that + subject + might/may + V1" expresses purpose, and the verb following the modal "might" must always be in its base form (V1), functioning as a verb — not a noun or adjective.

• "Success" is a noun and "successful" is an adjective; neither can grammatically follow the modal verb "might". The base verb form corresponding to the noun "success" is "succeed".

• Applying the rule: "so that I might succeed" correctly uses the base verb "succeed" after the modal "might" to express the purpose of working hard.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "that I may success" is incorrect because "success" (a noun) cannot follow the modal "may"; a base verb is required — also, since the main clause is in the past tense ("worked"), the modal should be "might", not "may".

• Option 2: "that I might successful" is incorrect because "successful" (an adjective) cannot follow the modal "might"; only a base verb (V1) can follow a modal.

• Option 4: "that I might successor" is incorrect because "successor" (a noun, meaning a person who succeeds another) cannot follow the modal "might", and it is also semantically wrong in this context.

NOTE

• Word family: succeed (verb) → success (noun) → successful (adjective) → successfully (adverb). Do not confuse "successor" (a person who follows another in a position) with "success".

• Sequence of tenses rule: when the main clause is in the past tense (e.g. "worked"), the subordinate purpose clause introduced by "so that" must use "might", not "may" (may is used when the main clause is in the present/future tense).

question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
A. The government's recent efforts have concentrated on strengthening these ties.
B. The textile industry in India is one of the country's oldest, stretching back several centuries.
C. The textile business is immensely diverse, with hand-spun and hand-woven textiles at one end of the spectrum and capital-intensive modern mills at the other.
D. Its tight ties to agriculture (for raw materials such as cotton) and the country's old history and traditions in terms of textiles set it apart from other sectors in the country.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. BCDA.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sentence B is the natural opener, introducing the topic — "The textile industry in India" — as a general, standalone statement about its age.

• Sentence C follows logically, elaborating on B by describing the diversity of the textile business (from hand-spun textiles to modern mills).

• Sentence D follows next, using the pronoun "Its" (referring back to the textile industry/business introduced in B and C) to describe its ties to agriculture and to the country's history and traditions.

• Sentence A concludes the paragraph: "these ties" directly refers back to the "tight ties to agriculture" mentioned in D, and describes the government's recent efforts to strengthen them.
◦ Logical chain: B (industry is old) → C (it is diverse) → D (it has ties to agriculture/history) → A (government strengthens these ties).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. BCDA.

Additional Information

• Option 1 (DABC) is incorrect because it opens with "Its tight ties to agriculture" — the pronoun "Its" has no antecedent at the very start of the paragraph.

• Option 2 (ABCD) is incorrect because it opens with "The government's recent efforts have concentrated on strengthening these ties" — "these ties" cannot be understood without the industry and its connections having been introduced first.

• Option 4 (CBDA) is incorrect because it opens with a description of diversity ("The textile business is immensely diverse") before the subject "the textile industry" and "the textile business" have been properly introduced by name in B — C reads awkwardly as an opener without B preceding it.

NOTE

• When solving para-jumbles, track pronouns (it, its, these, this, that, they) carefully — a sentence containing such a pronoun almost always follows the sentence that first names the noun it refers to.

• Look for a sentence that introduces the subject by name (here, "The textile industry in India") as the most likely opener of the paragraph.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Conceal
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Reveal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Conceal" means to keep something from being seen or known; to hide. (छिपाना)
◦ Example: She tried to conceal her disappointment behind a smile.

• "Reveal" means to make previously unknown or secret information known to others; to disclose. (उजागर करना, प्रकट करना) — this is the direct opposite of "conceal", making it the correct antonym.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Watch" means to look at something attentively — a verb of observation, not the opposite of hiding something.

• Option 2: "See" means to perceive with the eyes — again a verb of observation, not the opposite of "conceal".

• Option 4: "Hide" is actually a synonym of "conceal" (both mean to keep something out of sight), not its antonym.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "conceal": hide, cover up, disguise, mask, camouflage.

• Other antonyms of "conceal": disclose, expose, uncover, unveil, divulge — all of these mean to bring something into the open, exactly opposite to concealing it.

question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.
The stranger stood quietly for few moments.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. For a few moments.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Few" (without an article) means "not many; almost none", giving a negative sense, whereas "a few" (with the indefinite article "a") means "a small number; some", giving a positive sense.

• Rule: Before a plural countable noun like "moments", when a small positive quantity is meant (as here — the stranger did stand for some time), the article "a" must be used: "a few moments", not the bare "few moments" (which would suggest the stranger barely stood at all, an odd meaning here).

• The correct phrase is therefore "for a few moments", using the indefinite article "a" before "few".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "For the few moments" is incorrect because "the few moments" implies specific, previously identified moments (definite reference), which does not fit this general context.

• Option 2: "No improvement required" is incorrect because the original sentence "for few moments" (without "a") does carry the negative/near-zero sense of "few", which is not the intended meaning here — an improvement is needed.

• Option 3: "For moments" is incorrect because it drops "few" altogether, which is grammatically acceptable but changes the intended sense of a short, small duration; it does not correct the original error as precisely as "a few moments" does.

NOTE

• Key distinction: "few" (almost none, negative) vs "a few" (some, positive) — e.g. "Few people came" (implying disappointingly few) vs "A few people came" (implying some did come).

• The same distinction applies to uncountable nouns with "little" (almost none) vs "a little" (some) — e.g. "little water" (almost no water) vs "a little water" (some water).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Memory
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Oblivion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Memory" means the faculty of remembering; the state of being remembered. (स्मृति)
◦ Example: She has a photographic memory for faces.

• "Oblivion" means the state of being completely forgotten; unawareness. (विस्मृति, गुमनामी) — this is the direct opposite of "memory" (remembrance), making it the correct antonym.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Suppress" means to forcibly put an end to something or hold something back — it can describe suppressing a memory, but it is not itself the antonym of "memory".

• Option 3: "Retrospection" means the act of looking back on or reviewing past events — this is actually closely related to (not opposite of) memory, since it involves recalling the past.

• Option 4: "Impart" means to give or share information, knowledge or a quality with someone — unrelated to the sense of remembering or forgetting.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "memory": recollection, remembrance, retention, reminiscence.

• Other antonyms of "memory"/related word "remember": forget, disregard, obliviousness — "oblivion" is the noun form associated with the state of having forgotten or being forgotten entirely.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The civil service is an integral part of the government and plays a crucial role in implementing policies and programmes that benefit the public. The (1)_________ of civil services is to ensure that the government is able to provide services to citizens in a timely and effective manner. Civil servants are responsible for a wide range of tasks, including (2)_________ the implementation of policies and programmes, managing budgets and providing advice to government officials. In order to perform their duties effectively, civil servants must have a deep understanding of government processes, as well as strong (3)_________ and analytical skills. They must also be able to communicate effectively with a wide range of stakeholders, including government officials, citizens and other organisations. To become a civil servant, individuals typically need to pass a rigorous exam and undergo extensive training. Once they are appointed, civil servants are expected to abide by a code of conduct that emphasises impartiality, integrity and (4)_________ in carrying out their duties. Despite the challenges and demands of civil service work, it can be a highly rewarding career path, providing opportunities to make a positive impact on society and improve the lives of citizens. Whether working in a local, state or federal government agency, civil servants play a vital role in (5)_________ democratic values and promoting the public good.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. function.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires a word that means the purpose or role of civil services, since the sentence continues "...of civil services is to ensure that the government is able to provide services to citizens in a timely and effective manner" — a definition of what civil services are meant to do.

• "Function" means the natural or intended purpose/role of something, which fits perfectly: "The function of civil services is to ensure..." — describing the core purpose of civil services.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "mandate" means an official instruction or commission to act in a certain way; while related, it does not fit as naturally as "function" in describing the general purpose of an institution in this context.

• Option 2: "recommendation" means a suggestion or proposal about the best course of action — this does not fit the sense of describing the built-in purpose of civil services.

• Option 3: "defunct" means no longer existing, functioning, or in use — this is an adjective with a negative meaning that would make the sentence nonsensical ("The defunct of civil services..." is not even grammatically valid as a noun).

NOTE

• In cloze passages, always read the full sentence containing the blank (and often the sentences around it) to identify whether a noun, verb, or adjective is grammatically required, and then choose the option that best fits both the grammar and the overall meaning/tone of the passage.

• "Function" (role/purpose) should not be confused with "defunct" (no longer working) — despite the superficial similarity in spelling, their meanings are unrelated.

The civil service is an integral part of the government and plays a crucial role in implementing policies and programmes that benefit the public. The (1)_________ of civil services is to ensure that the government is able to provide services to citizens in a timely and effective manner. Civil servants are responsible for a wide range of tasks, including (2)_________ the implementation of policies and programmes, managing budgets and providing advice to government officials. In order to perform their duties effectively, civil servants must have a deep understanding of government processes, as well as strong (3)_________ and analytical skills. They must also be able to communicate effectively with a wide range of stakeholders, including government officials, citizens and other organisations. To become a civil servant, individuals typically need to pass a rigorous exam and undergo extensive training. Once they are appointed, civil servants are expected to abide by a code of conduct that emphasises impartiality, integrity and (4)_________ in carrying out their duties. Despite the challenges and demands of civil service work, it can be a highly rewarding career path, providing opportunities to make a positive impact on society and improve the lives of citizens. Whether working in a local, state or federal government agency, civil servants play a vital role in (5)_________ democratic values and promoting the public good.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. managing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence lists the tasks civil servants are responsible for: "...a wide range of tasks, including (2)_________ the implementation of policies and programmes, managing budgets and providing advice to government officials" — this is a list of three parallel gerund phrases (X-ing + object).

• Rule — Parallelism: In a list joined by commas and "and", all items must follow the same grammatical structure. Here the list already contains "managing budgets" and "providing advice", so the first item must also begin with a present-participle/gerund such as "managing": "managing the implementation..., managing budgets..., and providing advice...".

• "Managing" also fits the meaning best — civil servants oversee/manage the implementation of policies and programmes as part of their administrative duties.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "promoting" means encouraging or supporting something; while plausible in isolation, it does not fit the administrative/oversight sense of "the implementation of policies and programmes" as well as "managing" does.

• Option 2: "escalating" means to increase rapidly or intensify — this does not fit the meaning of overseeing implementation at all.

• Option 3: "developing" means creating or growing something; it could describe creating new policies, but the sentence is about handling the "implementation" of already-existing policies and programmes, which "managing" fits better.

NOTE

• Cloze questions frequently test parallel structure — when a blank is part of a list, check the grammatical form of the other items in the list (here, both other items use "-ing" verb forms) to identify the correct word form and, often, the correct word.

• Watch for near-synonyms in the options (managing/developing/promoting) — the correct choice is usually the one that best fits collocation and parallel structure, not merely one that is "not wrong" in isolation.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. problem-solving.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "...civil servants must have a deep understanding of government processes, as well as strong (3)_________ and analytical skills" — the blank must pair naturally with "analytical skills" as a commonly paired skill set.

• "Problem-solving" and "analytical" skills are a standard, frequently used collocation in professional/administrative contexts, referring to the ability to identify issues and work out logical solutions — exactly the kind of skill set expected of civil servants who must handle complex governance issues.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "technical" skills refer to specialised, often specific job-related expertise (e.g. IT, engineering); it does not pair as naturally with "analytical" in this general administrative context.

• Option 3: "interpersonal" skills relate to interacting with people (which the passage separately addresses in the next sentence about communicating with stakeholders); pairing "interpersonal and analytical" is less natural than "problem-solving and analytical", and would make the following sentence about communication redundant.

• Option 4: "accounting" skills are narrowly about financial record-keeping — too specific and not a natural pairing with general "analytical skills" in this broad description of a civil servant's required skill set.

NOTE

• "Problem-solving and analytical skills" is a fixed, frequently occurring collocation in professional/workplace English, commonly seen together in job descriptions and passages of this type — recognising common word pairings (collocations) is a key skill for cloze-passage questions.

• Distinguish "interpersonal skills" (dealing with people) from "problem-solving/analytical skills" (dealing with information and logic) — the passage addresses both separately, in different sentences.

solution_text:

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "...civil servants are expected to abide by a code of conduct that emphasises impartiality, integrity and (4)_________ in carrying out their duties" — the blank must complete a list of positive professional virtues expected of civil servants, alongside "impartiality" and "integrity".

• "Efficiency" means the ability to do something well, successfully and without wasted effort/resources, which is a natural third virtue alongside fairness (impartiality) and honesty (integrity) that a code of conduct for civil servants would emphasise.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "activism" means vigorous campaigning to bring about political or social change — this is not a professional virtue expected of a neutral civil servant carrying out duties under a code of conduct; in fact, civil servants are usually expected to remain apolitical.

• Option 4: "popularity" means being liked or admired by many people — this is not a virtue related to professional conduct/duty performance, and is out of place in a list about a code of conduct.

NOTE

• When a blank falls within a list of positive qualities (as with "impartiality, integrity and ___"), the missing word must share the same positive, professional tone as the surrounding items — immediately ruling out negative words like "severity" or irrelevant ones like "popularity"/"activism".

• Common civil-service code-of-conduct virtues frequently referenced in such passages: integrity, impartiality, objectivity, accountability, efficiency, transparency.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. upholding.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "...civil servants play a vital role in (5)_________ democratic values and promoting the public good" — the blank must pair naturally with "and promoting", forming a parallel positive-sense verb pair describing what civil servants do for democratic values.

• "Upholding" means supporting or defending something, especially a law, principle, or set of values, against attack or challenge, which fits perfectly with "democratic values" — civil servants are expected to uphold (protect/maintain) democratic values, just as they promote the public good.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "mimicking" means imitating or copying — this makes no logical sense in relation to "democratic values", which are meant to be upheld, not imitated.

• Option 3: "lacking" means being without something — this would give the sentence a negative meaning entirely opposite to the intended positive description of a civil servant's role, and pairs poorly with "and promoting" (a positive verb).

• Option 4: "contextualising" means placing something in its proper context or setting — this is an unusual and inappropriate collocation with "democratic values" in this context, and does not pair naturally with "and promoting".

NOTE

• "Upholding democratic values" and "promoting the public good" is a standard positive-sense collocation pair often seen in passages about governance, civil service, and public administration.

• As with Q.22, this blank is tested through parallel structure: the blank must match the positive tone and grammatical form ("-ing" verb) of "promoting" that follows it in the same clause.
